title: Parts of speech
examples: Teacher, what is the difference between an adjective and an adverb?
Can you give me more examples of verbs?
How do I know if a word is a pronoun?

explain.say: Today we will learn about parts of speech. These are word groups that give words jobs. We will look at five main jobs today. These jobs help us write clear sentences.

draw.text: Parts of Speech: Noun, Verb, Adjective, Adverb, Pronoun

explain.say: A noun is a person place thing or idea. For example, 'dog' is a noun. 'London' is a noun. 'happiness' is an idea noun. These words name things around us.

draw.text: Nouns name people, places, things, or ideas.

explain.say: A verb shows action or a state of being. For example, 'run' is an action verb. 'is' is a being verb. If you jump, 'jump' is the verb. Verbs tell us what is happening.

draw.text: Verbs show action or a state of being.

explain.say: An adjective describes a noun or pronoun. It tells us more about the thing. For example, the 'blue' car or the 'tall' student. Adjectives make our writing more detailed.
An adverb describes a verb adjective or another adverb. It often tells us how or when something happens. For example, she sang 'loudly'. 'Loudly' tells us how she sang.

draw.text: Adverbs describe how, when, or where.

faq.q: What is the difference between an adjective and an adverb?
faq.a: An adjective describes a noun, like a 'red' ball. An adverb describes an action, like rolling 'quickly'.
asks: How do I use adjectives and adverbs?
Does an adjective describe a verb?

faq.q: Are pronouns just names for people?
faq.a: No, pronouns take the place of nouns. Instead of saying 'Sarah went to the store', we say 'She went to the store.'
asks: Can I use a pronoun instead of a noun?

faq.q: Can a word be more than one part of speech?
faq.a: Yes, sometimes a word can act as different parts of speech. The job it does in the sentence decides what it is. For example, 'fast' can be an adjective or an adverb.
asks: Is it possible for one word to have many jobs?
How do I know which job a word is doing?

faq.q: What is the most important part of speech to know first?
faq.a: All parts of speech are important for building good sentences. However, knowing nouns and verbs helps you start building basic ideas.
asks: Which part of speech is the easiest to spot?
Do I need to know all of them at once?

faq.a: No, many adverbs do not end in -ly. Words like 'very' or 'now' are adverbs even without the -ly ending.
asks: Are there adverbs that don't use -ly?

facts: Nouns name people, places, things, or ideas.
Verbs show action or a state of being.
Adverbs often describe how an action happens.
Pronouns replace nouns to avoid repetition.

quiz.say: In the sentence 'The happy cat slept soundly', what part of speech is 'happy'?
quiz.why: The word 'happy' describes the noun 'cat'. Therefore, it is an adjective.

wrong.1: You might think it is a noun because it names a feeling.
wrong.2: You might think it is an adverb because it describes how the cat slept.
wrong.3: You might think it is a verb because it relates to the cat's state.

quiz.say: Identify the part of speech for the word 'she' in the sentence 'She jumped over the fence'.
quiz.why: The word 'she' takes the place of a person's name. This makes it a pronoun.

wrong.1: You might think it is a noun because it refers to a person.
wrong.2: You might think it is an adverb because it describes the action of jumping.
wrong.3: You might think it is an adjective because it seems to describe the jumping.

quiz.say: Which word is the verb in the sentence 'The little girl sang beautifully'?
quiz.why: The word 'sang' shows the action that the girl performed. Therefore, it is the verb.

wrong.1: You might choose 'little' because it describes the girl.
wrong.2: You might choose 'girl' because it is a person's name.
wrong.3: You might choose 'beautifully' because it describes how she sang.
